concept: Unsloth Desktop Studio macOS app running GGUF and MLX
summary: GGUF inference runs through llama.cpp; the loaded model is exposed as an authenticated API served by `llama-server`. MLX models run through an MLX backend on Apple Silicon (experimental since 2026-05-18, expanded since).

facts.text: GGUF inference runs through llama.cpp; the loaded model is exposed as an authenticated API served by `llama-server`. MLX models run through an MLX backend on Apple Silicon (experimental since 2026-05-18, expanded since).

API surface: Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` (for Claude Code, OpenClaw and the Anthropic SDK) and OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`. Keys are created in Settings, API, look like `sk-unsloth-...`, are shown once, and a revoked key returns 401.

`unsloth run --model <repo>:<quant>` loads a model with sampling, context, GPU-layer, threading, network and tool options, and prints an endpoint URL and API key. `unsloth studio -H 0.0.0.0 -p 8888` starts the web UI; the default bind is 127.0.0.1. `unsloth studio --secure` opens a free Cloudflare HTTPS tunnel.

Server-side tools (web search, Python and terminal execution) run as the local user and are on by default; anyone holding the API key can run code on the Mac, so `--disable-tools` is the guard when exposing the server. A preview OS-level tool sandbox exists on supported Linux and macOS hosts, with network access still unrestricted.

Model swapping: API requests can opt in to automatic switching between downloaded local GGUFs (2026-07-07); unknown model names keep using the current model. This makes Studio act like a llama-swap-style router.
Update mechanics: re-running the install command updates Studio; Desktop updates in-app.
2026-03-17: Studio beta launch (Mac behaved like CPU: chat first; the install page later says Data Recipes work and "MLX training now works").
2026-03-25: app shortcuts on macOS; Data Recipes on macOS and CPU.
2026-03-27 and 2026-04-01: auto-detect existing HF and LM Studio models, then user-selected folder.
2026-04-03: Intel Macs work.
2026-05-18: experimental MLX inference; API connections to OpenAI, Anthropic, vLLM, Ollama; MTP speculative decoding.
2026-05-19: "improve MTP not being faster on Macs, CPUs and GPUs".
2026-05-31: prebuilt llama.cpp binaries re-enabled for Apple Silicon M1-M4 on macOS 14, 15 and 26 (Tahoe); Apple Silicon on macOS 13 builds from source; Intel Macs on 13.3 to 26 use prebuilts.
2026-06-12: Studio uses fresh llama.cpp prebuilts across CUDA, ROCm, Windows, Linux and macOS; improved MLX model labels and generation speed stats.
2026-06-18: MLX training updates.
2026-07-07: macOS installs no longer need CMake or Homebrew when a prebuilt llama.cpp exists; Apple Silicon handling of paths with spaces and unified memory sizing improves.
2026-08-11: Unsloth Desktop (Beta) announced for Mac, Windows, Linux.
2026-08-20: custom llama.cpp build support; toggles for Cache RAM, Mmap, Mlock, Checkpoints, speculative-decoding KV cache and vision on/off.
2026-09-02: OpenAI-compatible APIs for video, audio and MLX-served models.
2026-09-17: MLX gains video input and optional MoE and decode optimizations.
2026-09-28: Apple Silicon improvements: batched serving, structured outputs and a TurboQuant KV cache.
2026-10-01 (release v0.1.902-beta): updated MLX support; Mac LoRA exports to PEFT or GGUF.

macOS floor: manual Studio install requires macOS 12 Monterey or newer and a Python environment (uv, venv or conda); prebuilt llama.cpp covers macOS 14, 15, 26 on Apple Silicon, so macOS 13 compiles llama.cpp from source.
The doc page for `unsloth run` shows the model argument `unsloth/qwen3.8-27B-GGUF-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL` with a doubled `-GGUF` suffix, which looks like a typo and would not resolve as written.

Mac training depth is contested: the install page says Studio works on Mac for chat and "training and all features" with MLX training working, while a third-party review says training is the weaker path on Mac and NVIDIA is listed for training.
Studio's Mac chat path historically lacked MLX tools and web search: the 2026-05-18 notes say "thinking, tools and web search soon" for MLX, so older MLX chats may not call tools.

Desktop uninstall (drag to Trash) leaves the Studio data and HF model cache; manual removal uses `rm -rf ~/.unsloth/studio`, the launcher `~/Applications/Unsloth Studio.app`, and `~/.local/bin/unsloth`.
`UNSLOTH_STUDIO_HOME` isolates a second install (own venv, auth, `studio.db`, cache and llama.cpp build).
Bundled llama.cpp can be stale: Studio warns when the prebuilt is too old for MTP.

What "Desktop" is relative to "Studio": Unsloth's docs call Desktop the easiest way to install Studio and a native app that Studio is packaged into; a third-party review calls Desktop a superset of Studio and says its CLI is `unsloth start`, while the Unsloth pages show `unsloth run` and `unsloth studio`. The docs are the primary source.
Licensing and telemetry are stated by a third-party review (Apache 2.0 core, AGPL-3.0 for Studio components, no telemetry) and not on the pages read from unsloth.ai; treat as unconfirmed.
Star count: review says about 70.2k, the GitHub releases page at fetch shows about 77.2k; the review is dated August.
No source compares Desktop's MLX decode and prefill speed to mlx-lm, LM Studio or oMLX on the same model and chip.
Which MLX build and mlx-lm version Desktop bundles, and how it pins them, is not stated.
How Desktop's "TurboQuant KV cache" differs from llama.cpp's q8_0 or q4_0 cache-type options is not documented in the changelog entry.
Unsloth Desktop (Beta) is a free, open-source app for running and training models on macOS, Windows and Linux, built on Tauri.
The Mac install is a `.dmg`: open it, drag Unsloth to Applications, launch and wait for installation to complete, then pick a model and quantization from the Select model dropdown or Model hub tab.
`curl -fsSL https://unsloth.ai/install.sh | sh` installs Unsloth Studio (the browser UI), not Desktop or Unsloth Core, and running it again updates.
`unsloth studio -H 0.0.0.0 -p 8888` launches Studio, and by default it binds to 127.0.0.1 only.
`unsloth studio --secure` launches over HTTPS through a free Cloudflare tunnel on Windows, Mac and Linux.
Studio's macOS requirement is macOS 12 Monterey or newer on Intel or Apple Silicon, inside a Python environment such as uv, venv or conda.
The install page says Mac chat and Data Recipes work and "MLX training now works", and the intro says Training, MLX and GGUF inference all work inside Unsloth on macOS.

Models loaded in Unsloth, including GGUFs, are exposed as an authenticated API through `llama-server`, with Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` and OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`.
API keys start with `sk-unsloth-`, are created under Settings, API, are shown only once, and revoked keys return 401.
`unsloth run` serves a model with context size, GPU layers, threading, sampling, networking and tool settings.
Server-side web search and Python and terminal execution run as the local user and are on by default; the install page says to pass `--disable-tools` when exposing Unsloth.
Unsloth Desktop lets users pick sandboxed tool execution or direct file access, and asks approval for file access outside the sandbox.
Studio can connect to OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, llama.cpp and vLLM backends and supports parallel chatting.
2026-05-18 changelog: experimental MLX inference lets MLX quants and models run on Macs, with thinking, tools and web search "coming soon".
2026-05-31 changelog: prebuilt llama.cpp binaries re-enabled for Apple Silicon (M1-M4) on macOS 14, 15 and 26; Apple Silicon on macOS 13 is a source build; Intel Macs use prebuilts.
2026-07-07 changelog: macOS installs no longer require CMake or Homebrew when a prebuilt llama.cpp is available, and Apple Silicon support handles paths with spaces and unified memory sizing better.
2026-07-07 changelog: API requests can opt into automatic switching between downloaded local GGUFs and `/v1/models` returns clean model IDs.
2026-08-20 changelog: custom llama.cpp builds and toggles for Cache RAM, Mmap, Mlock, Checkpoints, speculative-decoding KV cache and vision on/off.
2026-09-02 changelog: new OpenAI-compatible APIs for video, audio and MLX-served models.
2026-09-17 changelog: MLX gains video input, optional MoE and decode optimizations and more reliable multimodal chats; preview OS-level tool sandboxing arrives on supported Linux and macOS hosts.
2026-09-28 changelog: Apple Silicon improvements include batched serving, structured outputs and a TurboQuant KV cache.
2026-10-01 changelog (v0.1.902-beta): updated MLX support and Mac LoRA exports to PEFT or GGUF.
The 2026-08-11 changelog announces Unsloth Desktop for Mac, Windows and Linux supporting MLX, diffusion, audio and GGUF.

A Desktop uninstall is Finder, Applications, Move to Trash; manual Studio removal is `rm -rf ~/.unsloth/studio`, `rm -rf ~/Applications/Unsloth\ Studio.app` and `rm -f ~/.local/bin/unsloth`, and none of these touch downloaded HF model files.
Setting `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_HOME` installs Studio into an isolated location with its own virtual env, auth, `studio.db`, cache and llama.cpp build.

A third-party review states Unsloth Desktop ships Apache 2.0 core with AGPL-3.0 Studio components, no telemetry, and an `unsloth start` agent bridge, and calls Mac training "check before you plan around it".
On a Mac, Desktop's GGUF path is llama.cpp with Metal and its MLX path is a separate backend, so the same model can be run both ways in one app and compared for speed and fidelity locally.
